knowledge:
- key_parameters: object=A data frame, matrix, or SummarizedExperiment object with features (e.g., cluster-marker combinations) on the rows and samples as the columns ;; group_factor=A binary categorical response variable (0 and 1) representing the group condition for each sample ;; lowerRho=Optional positive value representing the lower bound of the kernel parameter (default is 2) ;; upperRho=Optional positive value representing the upper bound of the kernel parameter (default is 12) ;; gridRho=Optional positive value representing the number of grid points in the interval of upper and lower bounds of the kernel parameter (default is 4) ;; alpha=Optional significance level to control the False Discovery Rate (FDR) (default is 0.05) ;; featureVars=Optional vector of columns identifying features; if a SummarizedExperiment is used, row variables are used (default is NULL) ;; by=Parameter in CytoKDEData used to filter data (e.g., "features") ;; topK=Parameter in plotCytoK specifying the number of top differentially expressed features to plot
- alternatives: Linear models or analysis of variance (ANOVA), which may be insufficient to capture nonlinear relationships among co-expression features (e.g., signaling markers within and across cell subpopulations)
- when_to_use: When identifying differentially expressed features in high-dimensional biological experiments (e.g., CyTOF, flow cytometry, gene expression, RNA-Seq) where relationships among features are expected to be nonlinear
- pitfalls: The group_factor must be a binary categorical response variable (e.g., 0 and 1). Ensure the input data object has features on the rows and samples on the columns.

workflows.name: differential_expression_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify differentially expressed features in high-dimensional biological data using a kernel-based score test, filter the dataset, and visualize the top results.
input: expression_matrix.csv (matrix, data frame, or SummarizedExperiment of abundance measurements with features on rows and samples on columns)
group_labels.csv (binary categorical vector representing the group condition for each sample)
workflows.stages: 1. Run the kernel-based score test using CytoK() ;; 2. Extract all features, ordered features, and percentage of DE features using CytoKFeatures(), CytoKFeaturesOrdered(), and CytoKDEfeatures() ;; 3. Filter the original dataset to retain only differentially expressed features using CytoKDEData() ;; 4. Visualize the top differentially expressed features using plotCytoK() and ComplexHeatmap
workflows.code:
library(cytoKernel)
CytoK_output<- CytoK(cytoHDBMW,group_factor = rep(c(0, 1),
               c(4, 4)),lowerRho=2,upperRho=12,gridRho=4,
               alpha = 0.05,featureVars = NULL)
CytoK_output
head(CytoKFeatures(CytoK_output))
head(CytoKFeaturesOrdered(CytoK_output))
CytoKDEfeatures(CytoK_output)
CytoKDEData_HD<- CytoKDEData(CytoK_output, by = "features")
CytoKDEData_HD
heatmap1<- plotCytoK(CytoK_output,
group_factor = rep(c(0, 1), c(4, 4)),topK=10,
featureVars = NULL)
featureOrderedExtracted<- CytoKFeaturesOrdered(CytoK_output)
rowmeta_cluster<- featureOrderedExtracted$cluster
topK<- 10
rowmeta_clusterTopK<- rowmeta_cluster[seq_len(topK)]
library(ComplexHeatmap)
heatmap2<- Heatmap(rowmeta_clusterTopK,
             name = "cluster")
heatmap2+heatmap1
